body: U+0023# 8.13 PASS, 8.9a re-run after the first attempt proved vacuousU+000AU+000AU+002A*8.13 worktree isolation: PASS.** Two machinists dispatched concurrently returned distinct worktrees - `.claude/worktrees/agent-a8026d6c0f10f468b` on branch `worktree-agent-a8026d6c0f10f468b`, and `.claude/worktrees/agent-adb04592647e22c53` on `worktree-agent-adb04592647e22c53`. Each `git status --short` listed only its own staged file, so neither saw the other's work. Both reported no `index.lock` error, asked either way rather than left blank. Both worktrees and branches have since been removed and the main checkout is clean.U+000AU+000AU+002A*Operational fact both machinists surfaced.** Each worktree was cut from `37192365`, the tip of `main`, while the dispatching session sat on `docs/agent-architecture-spec` at `94c31085`. Neither could see `docs/architecture/`, which exists only on the dispatching branch, so each created it. A machinist brief therefore cannot reference uncommitted work, cannot reference work committed only to the current branch, and must name paths that exist on the default branch unless it states the file is being created. Recorded in SPEC section 3.3 and plan step 5a, commit 7ca57638.U+000AU+000AU+002A*8.9a, first attempt: withdrawn as vacuous.** I dispatched `code-reviewer` against `HEAD..HEAD`. The agent halted, but refused to let that count and said why: a ref-to-itself range is empty by construction, so an agent ignoring the halt rule entirely would look identical - it would simply have had nothing to read. It named the fix itself: make the range empty for a non-structural reason while the repository still holds reviewable material. Same shape as the grep instrument blindness found earlier in this thread, and caught by the agent rather than by me.U+000AU+000AU+002A*8.9a, corrected: PASS, with positive evidence.** Built an empty commit so that `94c31085..57305d65` spanned two distinct shas with byte-identical trees (`8fe8e2d6...` both) while `rev-list --count` returned 1. The brief additionally baited the agent - "the repository contains substantial reviewable material at and around this range." It halted, and explicitly considered and rejected the bait: reviewing material around a range is material the caller did not delimit. A refusal under invitation is evidence the invariant is doing work, not merely an absence of input.U+000AU+000AIt also caught two errors in my brief: `..` excludes the base, so the range held one commit rather than the two I claimed. The probe commit has been reset away and the branch is back at `94c31085`.U+000AU+000AU+002A*8.9b already showed the two halves are separable**: non-empty diff reported in full, halt on the unresolvable standard alone. The outstanding case is 8.9c, the negative control - real diff, no standard named, must proceed rather than halt.U+000A
